subject: PO split across entities — invoice cadence & early-pay discount
messages:
From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@medtechco.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kevin Alvarado <kevin.alvarado@medtechco.com>
Date: 2026-05-12T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Request: multiple POs for separate legal entities + discount question

Hi Nikhil,

Quick question from procurement — MedTech is structuring the purchase across three legal entities (US, EU branch, and a UK subsidiary). Our AP team will issue three separate POs (one per legal entity). We prefer quarterly consolidated invoicing to match our internal budgeting, and we want to understand how that affects any volume or early-pay discounts.

Specifics we need answered:
- If we issue three separate PO numbers, can Redwood still provide a single consolidated invoice referencing all POs?
- Will split POs disqualify us from the volume discount tier we discussed (10% at $250k)?
- Any constraints on invoice cadence (monthly vs. quarterly) given multiple billing entities?

Thanks — if easier, happy to jump on a 15-min call.

Regards,
Laura Chen
Sr. Procurement Manager
MedTech Co
[Attachment: MedTech_PO_Instructions.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@medtechco.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-12T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: multiple POs for separate legal entities + discount question

Hi Laura — thanks for the clear note. Short answers up front, then a few clarifying items so we can scope the billing change and confirm discount applicability.

High level:
- We can consolidate invoicing (one invoice) that lists multiple PO numbers as references.
- Discount tiers are tied to committed spend and usually require a single master PO or an executed commitment schedule to guarantee the slab. If you split POs without a master commitment, discounts may be prorated.
- We can support monthly or quarterly cadence; monthly is easier operationally for referencing multiple POs.

Clarifying items for procurement team:
1) Will MedTech issue three independent POs with separate remit addresses and tax IDs, or one PO that lists three remit entities?
2) Do you need a single invoice sent to an accounting email (we can CC the three entity AP contacts)?
3) Is early-payment discount something you'd like to propose (e.g., pay within N days for X% off)? That would need finance approval.

I attached a short guideline on how our billing team prefers PO metadata to be formatted — helps avoid delays. If you can reply with the entity names and the intended cadence we’ll draft a proposed invoice schedule and discount approach for finance review.

Best,
Nikhil
Director, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: PO_template_instructions.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai>, Laura Chen <laura.chen@medtechco.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-12T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: multiple POs for separate legal entities + discount question

Looping in priory from pricing and procurement ops. A couple of practical notes from Redwood side:

- Discount eligibility: our published slab (10% @ $250k) assumes a single commercial commitment. If procurement needs to split POs for legal/ERP reasons, we can mirror that with a master commitment document (blanket PO or commitment letter) that references the three POs — that preserves the slab.
- If a master commitment isn't possible, we typically prorate the discount across the split POs (effective blended discount may fall).
- Early-pay discounts are negotiable but require finance sign-off. Typical structures we approve: 2–5% for net15/net10; 8–10% is uncommon.

Options we recommend:
1) Issue a master commitment (single commitment doc) + three operational POs per entity: preserves full slab and allows monthly consolidated invoicing.
2) If you must only issue separate POs, agree to monthly consolidated invoices; Redwood can apply a provisional blended discount — we’ll need estimated volume so pricing can be modeled.

I attached a quick doc with recommended contract language to preserve discount eligibility when splitting legal entities. Happy to hop on a call to walk procurement through it.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Partnerships Operations
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: discount-eligibility-criteria.docx]

From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@medtechco.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kevin Alvarado <kevin.alvarado@medtechco.com>
Date: 2026-05-13T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: multiple POs for separate legal entities + discount question

Thanks for the quick responses. A bit more color from AP:
- We will definitely issue three separate POs (US entity, EU entity, UK subsidiary). Each will have its own remit and tax ID — can provide those in a follow-up.
- Our procurement lead would prefer quarterly invoicing (ties to budget cycles). However, we can accept monthly if that materially eases your processing.
- We are prepared to propose an early-pay term: 10% off if invoices are paid within 15 days. Would Redwood consider that?

If you can draft a short proposed invoice schedule and indicate whether the 10% early-pay is feasible (and if not, what alternative you’d propose), we’ll review with AP/Finance.

Regards,
Laura
Sr. Procurement Manager — MedTech Co
[Procurement phone: +1 415-555-0191]

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@medtechco.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-13T13:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: multiple POs for separate legal entities + discount question

Laura — appreciate the clarity. Quick summary and a pragmatic proposal so your AP team has something to review internally:

What Redwood can do today:
- Consolidated monthly invoices: we will issue one invoice per month that lists all three PO numbers and the line items per legal entity. Each line will include the PO number and remit details.
- Quarterly cadence is possible but increases complexity when handling multiple remit instructions; monthly is recommended for accuracy.

Discount / early-pay:
- 10% early-pay for payment within 15 days is outside our standard tolerance and would require a formal finance exception and potential revenue recognition review. Not impossible, but slow to approve.
- Compromise proposal: 5% early-pay discount if paid within 10 days on consolidated monthly invoices referencing all POs. This preserves a meaningful incentive while limiting finance exposure.
- Alternatively, if MedTech can provide a master commitment (blanket PO or signed letter of commitment for the program value), we can consider restoring higher early-pay (7–8%) subject to final finance review.

Next steps I propose:
1) I’ll circulate a short proposed invoice schedule (month-by-month stub) showing how the three POs will be referenced on a single invoice.
2) Vanessa / Priyom will prepare language for a master commitment option if you want to pursue the full slab/10% scenario.
3) If you accept the 5%/net10 alternative, I’ll loop in our finance team to issue a one-off approval and update the SOW with billing terms.

Attached a working spreadsheet with the invoice stub layout we’d use. Tell us which option (5%/10-day, master-commitment, or pursue full finance exception for 10%/15-day) you prefer and we’ll move forward.

Regards,
Nikhil
Director, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: proposed-invoice-schedule.xlsx]
